text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Six hundred illiegal migrants housed in a refugee camp in the eastern Lithuanian town of Pabrade went on a riot on Wednesday to protest new regulations restricting their movement outside of the camp. Calm was restored after authorities agreed to negotiate.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas and his Russian counterpart Boris Yeltsin discussed bilateral relations in a telephone conversation on Wednesday.
- The parliamentary justice committee has introduced a motion to abolish capital punishment.
- The Lithuanian Develompment Bank and Vilniaus Bank issued a joint $3.9 million credit to Medienos Plaushas to upgrade its production lines.
- Price Waterhouse was chosen by the finance ministry to evaluate the State Commercial Bank, which has been slated for privatisation.
- Lithuania's Social Democrats registered an initiative group on Wednesday to organise a referendum on the opposing the privatisation of key state assets.
- Per capita income was 345 litas in Lithuania in the first quarter of the year, but to satisfy all major needs a sum of 630 litas is necessary, the statistics department said.
